checks.why: The HttpApi has no browser clients and the PR adds no CORS config.
The new route is a POST that returns 202; no caching is involved.
No migrations or flags; the SAM stack can be rolled back as a whole. Events already queued would be left for the old consumer.

The function Timeout is 10 s and the Mailer can sleep 7 s per record. At BatchSize 10 the worst case is 70 s, which is over the function timeout; the queue visibility timeout is the 30 s default, which is not six times the timeout.
No metrics or labels are added.
Exact-day equality windows and a `today()` taken at delivery time.
Lambdas have no health endpoints, and none are needed.
There is no background work to flush.
The HttpApi has no throttle, and `/remind` can mail the same loan on every authenticated call.
No alarms for consumer errors, queue age or DLQ depth anywhere in the infrastructure code.

probes.claim: With a Mailer whose outbox.append raises OSError every time, `consumer.handle` returns normally after 7 s of sleep and sets `reminded_on`; `/remind` still returns 202.
A batch of 10 records where record 6 raises KeyError sends 5 mails on each delivery, so after N deliveries the first 5 members get 5N mails.
A loan with `returned_on` set and a `loan.overdue` event still produces 1 overdue mail.
`send_reminders` run on day D-1 and D+1 but not on D reminds 0 of the loans due at D+2 (exact-day equality).
